newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends lower in slow range-bound trading.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends lower in slow range-bound trading.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures ended weaker in continued slow range-bound activity as traders marked time ahead of the August 12 USDA crop report.

"It was really slow. The speculators continue to be on the short side and the trade was a scale down buyer," a dealer said, adding, "It appears that traders are neutralizing their positions ahead of the August 12 crop report," he said.

"The market will be watching for the estimate," said Texas A and M University cotton specialist Carl Anderson. He noted the estimates were coming in close to expectations of a 18-million-bale crop for 1997/98 season which began August 1.
Last year's crop was 18.94 million bales.
"The acreage is down from 14.63 million planted to 14 million acres planted this year," Anderson added.
Most active December cotton lost 0.14 cent to end at 74.70 cents a lb while the rest of the board was 0.05 firmer to 0.23 lower.
Volume was thin to moderate, about 5,000 lots changed hands, a cotton trader said.
